Intresting so using ways + 1 mmap or virtual alloc (4096 aligned) will cause eviction on the L1 cache. To utilize the full L1 cache we need to use the number of ways of mmap/virtual alloc. To Avoid thrashing we can reuse mmap or virtual alloc
Each 64 byte offset of 4096 will map to the next set
So the hardware prefetches in set not ways

On AMD Zen processors, the L1D cache is
virtually indexed and physically tagged (VIPT). 
So we use the offset (use to point to the first byte in cache)  +
  index which is used to get the set in the cache
Both use the virtual address

 we use the tag to get the specific way in a given set
uses the physical address

Thoughts:
Do we need to store the indices in a mmap? or can we make due with just storing a QWORD to hold the current indice?
Do we need to store all the indices and keep track????? if not than we can get rid of the indices array and just make due with a QWORD


I Don't think we need to store all the indices in a collection, but rather we just need to store the current indice in a QWORD and increment this.

Assuming that we are just have Indices array in cache. We can only hold 294912 indices (entities) before we start evicting the L1 cache. This is not what we really want, since we want to support alot of indices without evicting the cache because we are hold presistent data. If we are including other allocation and the stack the 294912 indices before evicting will actually be a lot less.
Is it worth the trade off? No...... 
So we will store the current indice rather than a collection of indices to avoid page faults and cache evictions.
